Summary
02 / 34
Summary 2026 to date
Expansion: found the right entry points for a full Nordic build-out and the UK expansion, phase 1.
Operational development: Picoway implementations, protocols, training and onboarding, and overall unification of the offering and ways of working.
Platform: Beam-aligned workflows in the clinic and integrations across the full tech stack.
Regional management: introducing regional management and defined overhead requirements to allow for group-focused growth come 2027.
Capacity build-out: refits (The Hague, AMS 1), additional lasers (Utrecht, Overtoom, The Hague, STO 1) and new hires at 7 clinics.
Brand development: all local brands are coming into one.

CEO view
  • Demand for tattoo removal is weaker than planned, in every market; it is the main reason growth is below plan. 
  • Plan was to offset weak demand with group driven marketing, but merger completion has held initiatives back on awareness.  
  • Q3 re-focus: adding capacity in current clinics, and integrating all entities.
What moved the numbers operationally
  • Norway: laser fault on 2 June; treatments far lower until 2 September. Operational, not demand.
  • Sweden: more customers prepaying packages and full-removal plans (CRP); revenue per treatment up, some sessions still to deliver.
  • UK – TRUK: pipeline rebuilding after marketing was held back in H1.

Integration Update
Performance
Organisation
Integration
Expansion
16 / 34
Information
Since March we have rebuilt Beam around clinical excellence: one platform and one data model for every market
Six markets on one model by 1 December. Each new clinic group becomes a data migration and a configuration, not a new build.
What we have built since March
Treatment plans: one plan per client, tattoo and removal journey, priced and consented up front, so clinics sell the full removal journey.
Clinic-floor flow: intake review, phone photos, laser safety check and checkout in one visit view. More effective treatments, complete medical records, accurate admin.
Packages and payments: packages, instalments, gift cards and products in one POS, with one purchase journal and VAT per country behind every balance.
Booking and calendars: one calendar for online and in-clinic booking, drag-and-drop rescheduling, and gap-filling slot selection ready to switch on.
Follow-up and KPIs: notes, tasks and call lists keep clients from slipping between visits. One dashboard shows conversion, utilisation and documentation per clinic.
One data model, every market
Same core everywhere: client, plan, booking, session, package and payment mean the same in every market. Prices, VAT, language, brand and booking rules are settings, not code.
Four systems already mapped in: Timely (UK – TRUK), Timma (Norway), old Beam (Sweden), and Salonized plus clinic workbooks (Netherlands, ~21 Oct).
Built in modules, to adapt to local requirements: Local regulatory and operational requirements can be adapted to each respective region. 
Local data, group view: each country keeps its own database. A group layer links clients across markets and adds up the KPIs on one definition.
Long-term value
Lower cost per acquisition
Improvements reach every clinic at once
Comparable numbers: conversion, utilisation and retention are measured the same way in every clinic, so pricing, capacity and investment decisions rest on like-for-like data.
A clinical data asset: settings, photos, reactions and outcomes for every treatment in one structure. The base for better session estimates, pricing and AI support.
Owned: replaces Timely, Timma, Salonized, pCloud and Microsoft Office, and the roadmap is ours.
Owned: replaces Timely, Timma, Salonized, pCloud and Microsoft Office, and the roadmap is ours.
Connected and MCP-driven: connect directly with all integrated systems in real time.

Appendix D · Definitions and sources
How the operating figures are counted
34 / 34
Consultations: customers with a completed consultation in the period, earliest counting. Netherlands: the intake.
Conversion: share of those with a treatment planned or done on or after the consultation day.
Treatments: completed treatment visits, one per customer and day.
Came back ≤180 days: treatment visits followed by another within 180 days; only visits whose 180 days have passed (Jan–Mar).
CAC: marketing spend over new customers, Growth report definitions.
Beam (Sweden & Denmark, Norway, UK – TRUK), read 7 October 2026. Norway history before 30 September 2026 imported from Timma; TRUK before 17 August 2026 from Timely.
Salonized export for the Netherlands, 1 October 2026.
Growth report: Network Performance Report (Head of Growth), final. Used for new customers, marketing spend and CAC only.
Revenue and profit are reported only in Financials, from the management accounts. Operating sources measure revenue differently and are not shown.
